ei.title: Children and the Principle of Opposites
ei.subject: 10월 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Children and the Principle of Opposites

fullPassage:
As children, the principle of opposites is foreign. Children perceive words and their meanings separately from each other. It is only in later development that we understood that individual words directly connect to one another.

For many children, for instance, it is not clear that 'Right' is the opposite of 'Left'. A vivid example of this can be seen when children learn to ride a bicycle. If parents tell their child "Don't go to the left," they will often find that the child will continue riding straight ahead and not automatically turn to the right.

The same applies to the logical connection between 'Yes' and 'No' as perceived by parents. When we were children and were told, for example, "No, don't eat with your hands," we were confused and didn't know what our parents expected from us.

Our confusion was about whether we should continue eating or not and if so, how? Only later did we recognize the connection and understand that we should continue eating, but not with our hands but with a fork or a spoon.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② tells → tell: 주어 parents가 복수이므로 동사에 -s를 붙이지 않은 tell
det.analysis:
✅ ① perceive: 적절 — 복수 주어 Children에 맞춘 복수동사 perceive
❌ ② tells → tell: 주어 parents(부모, 복수)이므로 3인칭 단수형 tells가 아니라 tell이 되어야 함 ←정답

det.tip: 복수 주어(parents) + 현재시제 → 동사원형 (parents tell)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

If parents tell their child "Don't go to the left," they will often find that the child will continue riding straight ahead and not automatically turn to the right.

The same applies to the logical connection between 'Yes' and 'No' as perceived by parents. When we were children and were told, for example, "No, don't eat with your hands," we were ③<u>confused</u> and didn't know what our parents expected from us.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② the synonym of(~의 동의어) → the opposite of(~의 반대말): 'Right'는 'Left'의 반대말
det.analysis:
✅ ① meanings: 적절 — 아이들은 단어와 그 '의미'를 별개로 인식함
❌ ② the synonym of → the opposite of: 이 글은 반대말의 원리를 다루며, 'Right(오른쪽)'는 'Left(왼쪽)'의 동의어(synonym)가 아니라 '반대말(opposite)'임 ←정답
✅ ③ confused: 적절 — 부모의 기대를 몰라 '혼란스러웠음'
✅ ④ spoon: 적절 — 손이 아니라 포크나 '숟가락'으로 먹어야 함
det.tip: 글의 핵심 소재 = the principle of opposites(반대말의 원리)

questions.passage:
As children, the principle of opposites is foreign. Children perceive words and their meanings separately from each other. It is only in later development that we understood that individual words directly connect to one another.

For many children, for instance, it is not clear that 'Right' is the opposite of 'Left'. A vivid example of this can be seen when children learn to ride a bicycle. If parents tell their child "Don't go to the left," they will often find that the child will continue riding straight ahead and not automatically turn to the right.

The same applies to the logical connection between 'Yes' and 'No' as perceived by parents. When we were children and were told, for example, "No, don't eat with your hands," we were confused and didn't know what our parents expected from us.

Our confusion was about whether we should continue eating or not and if so, how? Only later did we recognize the connection and understand that we should continue eating, but not with our hands but with a fork or a spoon.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 원문: Only later did we recognize the connection — '나중에야' 깨달았지, 듣는 순간 곧바로 깨달은 것이 아님
det.analysis:
✅ ① 아이들은 단어와 의미를 서로 별개로 인식한다는 원문과 일치
✅ ② 많은 아이들에게 'Right'가 'Left'의 반대라는 것이 분명하지 않다는 원문과 일치
✅ ③ 우리의 혼란은 계속 먹어야 할지 말아야 할지에 대한 것이었다는 원문과 일치
❌ ④ 손이 아니라 포크나 숟가락으로 먹어야 한다는 것은 '나중에야(Only later)' 깨달았다고 했으므로 '듣는 순간 곧바로 깨달았다'는 불일치 ←정답
det.tip: Only later did we recognize ~ = 나중에야 비로소 깨달았다

ch: 발달 초기의 아이들은 단어와 그 의미를 서로 별개의 것으로 받아들인다.
